answer: Texas uses electronic titles, so your lender sends the lien release to the state electronically rather than as a paper title document, and there's no paper title to bring because we transfer the title electronically at the appointment. The lien still has to be released, so ask your bank for a lien release letter. If you can't get one, sign the lien release request (form NW-LRL-1) and we'll contact the lender for you, which can add 1 to 2 weeks. You don't have to wait for the release: we can still make you an offer and book your appointment in the meantime.
